title: Prepending a Left Memory Move
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}:\{0,1,2,3\}\to\{0,1\}^*\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be an oracle, and let $x$ be a Boolean word. Let $st$ be a machine state whose 17 register values are all at most $B$, let $M:\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a memory, let $p\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy $0\le p\le P$, and let $l,l'$ be control states. If the instruction at $l$ moves the memory head one cell left and continues at $l'$, then every guarded finite run from the configuration at $l'$ with state $st$, memory $M$, and head position $p-1$ to a configuration $c$ can be prefixed by that instruction: there is a guarded finite run from the configuration at $l$ with the same state and memory and head position $p$ to $c$.
hypotheses_covered: an oracle on four indices and Boolean words
a state $st$ with all 17 register values at most $B$
the instruction at $l$ is a left memory move to $l'$
guarded reachability from the specified successor configuration to $c$
replaced:
Fix $K_0$, an oracle $O$, a Boolean input $x$, and natural-number bounds $B,P$. Let $S$
be a register state, $M$ an integer-indexed Boolean memory, $p$ an integer, $l,l'$
machine states, and $c$ a machine configuration. If the instruction at $l$ is a move of
the memory head one cell to the left followed by state $l'$, every register of $S$ is at
most $B$, and $0\le p\le P$, then any guarded reachability of $c$ from the configuration
in state $l'$ with memory head at $p-1$ implies guarded reachability of $c$ from the
configuration in state $l$ with memory head at $p$.
